title: Instructions and data registers
summary: The TAP becomes useful through its **instructions**: they choose a data register and a mode of the chip. This topic covers the standard instructions, the BYPASS and IDCODE registers, the exact TMS sequence that loads an instruction, and how several chips share one JTAG chain.
objectives: List the mandatory and common optional 1149.1 instructions.
Explain BYPASS and the fields of IDCODE.
Write the TMS sequence that loads an instruction or shifts a data register.
Compute the scan length of a chain of several chips.

blocks.caption: IEEE 1149.1 instructions

blocks.title: A check built into the IR
blocks.md: During Capture-IR the instruction register always loads a pattern ending in **…01**. A tester shifting out the IR sees this 01 for every chip — a quick check that the chain is connected and of the expected length.

**BYPASS** is a single flip-flop. With BYPASS selected, a chip adds only **one bit** to the scan path, so a tester can reach one chip on a board without shifting through all the others.

**IDCODE** is a 32-bit read-only register that tells the tester which chip it is talking to:

blocks.caption: IDCODE fields: version, part number, JEDEC manufacturer code, and a constant 1

blocks.title: After reset
blocks.md: Test-Logic-Reset selects IDCODE if the chip has one, otherwise BYPASS. BYPASS captures 0, IDCODE starts with bit 0 = 1. So after a reset the tester can shift out the whole chain and **discover** every chip on the board.

rows: n−1 times 0, then 1 on the last bit (→ Exit1)
blocks.caption: TMS recipes every JTAG driver uses

blocks.prompt: Practice: starting in Run-Test/Idle, put the states of an instruction load in order.

blocks.md: On a board, all chips share **TCK** and **TMS**; their TDI and TDO are connected in a **daisy chain**: TDO of one chip goes to TDI of the next. All TAP controllers walk through the same states together; the instruction and data registers of all chips form one long shift path.

blocks.caption: Reading the IDCODE of chip 2: the other chips are bypassed

blocks.title: The same idea inside a chip
blocks.md: Choosing which registers are in the path — and keeping the others out — is exactly what IJTAG does **inside** a chip with its segment insertion bits (Topic 6).
